title: Add `.getbatch` to dataloaders that inherits mnist_dataset
description:
As `torchvision::mnist_dataset()` will [eventually](https://github.com/mlverse/torchvision/issue/309) get a .getbatch() method,  this pull request overide .getbatch() when requires in luz exemples.

I fully agree that the code looks awful for a pedagogic example, but as we don't (want to ) add a torchvision>= 0.9 constraint, we need exemples using mnist_dataset() to have
- redefinition of .getitem(), used by users with torchvision <= 0.8 
- redefinition of .getbatch(), used by users with torchvision >= 0.9 

This is an alternative fix for https://github.com/mlverse/torchvision/issues/263 with `torchvision::mnist_dataset()` having `.getbatch()` method.

title: Add scheduler reduce on plateau
description:
Hi there, I recently came across a small hiccup while using the `luz` package (kudos on the great work! 😃). It seems that when attempting to employ the `reduce_on_plateau` learning rate scheduler, an exception is triggered due to the `luz_callback_lr_scheduler` not factoring in the `current_loss` for specific schedulers. 
This issue bears a resemblance to a similar one I encountered in the tabnet package, https://github.com/mlverse/tabnet/pull/120). I've crafted a corresponding solution and submitted this pull request to solve this bug.
Please let me know if there's anything else I can provide or do to support this pull request.

title: Autoresume
description:
This callback will allow luz models to auto-resume in case of failure.
The idea is:

- User adds the `luz_callback_auto_resume()`
- Run the script
- If the script fails for some random reason, you can resume training from where it stopped by simply re-running the same script. Metrics, model parameters and optimizer state is automatically ported from the previous run.

Caveats:

- Tracking state of model runs is hard: we are currently tracking the optimizer state and the model state. If you need to track the state of other callbacks (eg. learning rate schedulers), we will provide an extension interface for that, but user will need to write custom code.
- There's no way for us to make sure the model the user is trying to resume is the same that has failed. It's user responsibility to make sure they didn't modify the code between runs.

Fix #88

title: Add backward argument to `setup`.
description:
This allows one to customize how to call `backward()`, for example, if you want to call backward with `create_graph=TRUE` you can use:

```
mod <- model %>%
    setup(
      loss = torch::nn_mse_loss(),
      optimizer = torch::optim_adam,
      backward = function(x) {
        x$backward(create_graph = TRUE)
      }
    )
```

title: Add callback for gradient clipping inspired by FastAI's.
Update learning rate exponentially and maybe, add smoothing to loss plot
description:
First proposal of implementing a smoothed display of the loss, as done here: https://sgugger.github.io/how-do-you-find-a-good-learning-rate.html and (1:1 translation to R) here: https://blogs.rstudio.com/ai/posts/2020-10-19-torch-image-classification/.

From practical experience, this should be more helpful to most users.

Implementation-wise, it seems like it has to go into `plot.lr_records`, in which case I don't really know how we would want to make it configurable (in a useful way) ... For now, just so one can compare, I've added arguments `smoothed_loss` and `beta` to this method.

Here are example plots of smoothed vs. non-smoothed loss:

```
> df <- data.frame(lr = exp(1:100), loss=rep(c(150, 1000, 50, 10, 1), 20))
> plot.lr_records(df, smoothed_loss = FALSE)
> plot.lr_records(df)
```

title: Bugfix/early stopping
description:
This PR fixes 2 issues:

1. early stopping would always happen in the first epoch if patience = 1 because we would compare the metric with itself- meaning that there was no improvement and then we stopped. This now fixed by simply skipping the early stopping logic when in the first epoch. Fix #63 

2. We can now control the `weight` of a callback, ie the order it should be called in the callback list. Callbacks with no weight attribute are called in the same order they are specified. Early stopping is now a callback with `weight = Inf` meaning that its the last callback to be called. Fix #64 

We also moved much of the code for the early stopping callback to a different file, so it's easier to test and navigate.

title: Implements `evaluate`
description:
This PR has taken a small detour and we are now implementing checking for `ctx` assignments too.
The idea is to be able to simplify the `fitted` object so `evaluate` and `predict` can create their own new `context` that would never modify the `fitted` object by accident.

- The context object is no longer retained after training: this allows us to keep the output much cleaner as well as having better control on what is accessible in the output.
- The context object is now locked: it's harder to make strange assumptions regarding the context.
- Context fields are now `active` fields and we provide checks for the most important ones.
- We have implemented an `evaluate` function that allows evaluating a fitted model.

title: Feature/yardstick
description:
@mattwarkentin I have played with the idea we discussed in #6  using `yardstick` here.

The problems I see are:

-  for example: `accuracy` in yardstick expects factors while torch don't know about factors at all. 
- Matrixes are not supported, while it's quite common that your model returns `(batch_size, 1)` predictions. I think this enough for us to re-implement stuff in luz.

I tried to fix these by allowing a `transform` function that is called before trying to apply the metrics, so the user has control on how to transform predictions and targets before passing to yardstick.

What do you think?
